introduction: ERC-5484 defines an interface extending ERC-721 to create consensual soulbound tokens (SBTs): non-transferable NFTs whose burn permission is agreed by both parties before issuance. It was proposed by Buzz Cai in August 2022. Before issuance, the issuer and receiver agree on a burn authorization — IssuerOnly, OwnerOnly, Both, or Neither — that is immutable afterward. The contract emits an Issued event alongside the ERC-721 Transfer event and exposes a burnAuth query that tells SBTs apart from ordinary NFTs.
designPurpose: ERC-5484 was designed to give soulbound tokens a shared interface so wallets, explorers, and services can treat them consistently. Earlier soulbound implementations extended ERC-721 but simply reverted on every transfer, with no standard way to detect non-transferability or learn who may destroy the token. ERC-5484 fixes a per-token burn authorization at issuance, requires the receiver's consent beforehand, and adds a burnAuth getter plus an Issued event so third parties can identify them through ERC-165 detection.
commonUsage: Consensual soulbound tokens are intended for credentials, memberships, certifications, and credit records — cases where a token should stay bound to one address rather than trade freely. The burn authorization is chosen per use case: IssuerOnly suits revocable loan records, OwnerOnly suits memberships the holder can discard, Both suits credentials, and Neither suits permanent credit history. Because SBTs remain ERC-721 tokens, existing NFT tooling can display them while checking the interface before any transfer.
fn.burnAuth.desc: Returns the burn authorization for a token, indicating which parties may destroy it: IssuerOnly, OwnerOnly, Both, or Neither. Queries for unassigned token IDs revert.
fn.burnAuth.params.tokenId: The identifier of the token to query.
fn.burnAuth.returns.burnAuth: The immutable burn authorization fixed for the token at issuance.
fn.Issued.desc: Emitted when a soulbound token is issued, in addition to the ERC-721 Transfer event, so third parties can distinguish an SBT issuance from an ordinary NFT transfer.
fn.Issued.params.tokenId: The identifier of the issued token.
fn.Issued.params.burnAuth: The burn authorization agreed for this token, fixed at issuance.
sim.issueTokenWalkthrough.name: Issue Soulbound Token
sim.issueTokenWalkthrough.desc: Follow the issuance of a consensual soulbound token, from the issuer through storage and the Issued event to a burnAuth query.
sim.issueTokenWalkthrough.step.issue: The issuer issues a soulbound token to the receiver, who has already consented to the chosen burn authorization.
sim.issueTokenWalkthrough.step.store: The contract records the immutable burn authorization for the token and assigns ownership to the receiver.
sim.issueTokenWalkthrough.step.event: The contract emits Issued(from, to, tokenId, burnAuth) alongside the ERC-721 Transfer event to flag the SBT issuance.
sim.issueTokenWalkthrough.step.query: A third party calls burnAuth(tokenId) to read which party is allowed to burn the token before acting on it.
